title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 52
paragraphs: So the Persians, taking up position on the rising ground opposite the Acropolis — which the Athenians call the Hill of Ares — began to besiege them in this way: they put tow around their arrows, set it alight, and shot them against the palisade. The besieged Athenians continued to defend themselves nonetheless, though they had come to the extremity of distress and their palisade had failed them; nor would they accept terms of surrender when the sons of Peisistratos brought them forward. In their defense they devised several contrivances against the enemy — among other things, they rolled down great stones when the barbarians approached the gates — so that for a long time Xerxes was at a loss, unable to capture them.
